description.text: Headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee, FedEx Freight is the largest North American less-than-truckload (“LTL”) freight carrier, with industry-leading transit times and service levels, offering choice, simplicity, and reliability to meet the needs of LTL shippers while operating ethically with a commitment to “Safety Above All.” As of June 1, 2026, we had approximately 40,000 employees, over 365 locations, including approximately 355 shipping terminals (over 320 of which are in the United States) and approximately 10 linehaul relay sites, and nearly 30,000 motorized vehicles, of which nearly 17,000 are tractors, across all 50 U.S. states, Canada, and Mexico. We also offer freight delivery service to most points in Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Our robust network established through almost 60 years of operations and consisting of more than 26,000 service center doors strategically positioned in high-demand regions provides critical services that facilitate the transport of goods in North America and powers the supply chains of our customers. Our services and solutions support companies of all sizes, industries, and specialties, and our proximity to our customers allows us to transport their goods quickly, reliably, and efficiently.

about.description_short: FedEx Freight is North America's largest less-than-truckload (LTL) carrier, delivering industry-leading published transit times, service levels, and reliability. FedEx Freight's service offerings - including Priority, Economy, and Direct - allow customers to balance speed and cost to meet their unique needs. FedEx Custom Critical, a subsidiary, provides expedited, time- and temperature-specific freight solutions, including Surface Expedite and White Glove Services, available 24/7/365. With nearly 30,000 vehicles, of which nearly 17,000 are tractors, and 40,000 dedicated team members to support its network of over 365 locations, we ensure freight arrives safely, securely, and on time across all 50 U.S. states, Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. FedEx Freight leverages operational efficiency, data-driven technology, and a focused sales organization to provide outstanding service.

employees.evidence: As of June 1, 2026, we had approximately 40,000 employees, and our exceptional network shapes our identity, reputation, and the type of business we strive to be.

analysis_md:
# FDXF — FedEx Freight Holding Company, Inc.
v5.4 run, 2026-10-16 (first pass). All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The largest North American less-than-truckload (LTL) carrier — Priority / Economy / Direct services, ~86,000 average daily shipments, ~365+ locations, more than 26,000 service-center doors, nearly 30,000 vehicles, ~40,000 employees, serving 98% of U.S. ZIP codes plus Canada and Mexico. Spun off from FedEx Corporation on June 1, 2026: 80.1% of shares distributed to FedEx holders (1 FDXF share per 2 FDX shares), FedEx retained a 19.9% stake it expects to monetize within 24 months, and FDXF funded a ~$4.1B pre-separation cash dividend to FedEx with new debt. Fiscal year-end changed from May 31 to December 31 effective June 1, 2026, so the period June–December 2026 is a seven-month transition period. Market cap $16.98B at $113.58 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

## Owner's earnings
**History is carve-out only — 3 fiscal years** (financials_history.csv, 10-K filed 2026-08-05):

| FY (ended May 31) | Revenue | Operating income | OCF | Capex | SBC | Conservative OE | OE/share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | $9,424M | $1,753M | $1,541M | $461M | $12M | $1,068M | $7.14 |
| 2025 | $8,892M | $1,404M | $1,531M | $437M | $10M | $1,084M | $7.25 |
| 2026 | $8,795M | $540M | $167M | $379M | $13M | −$225M | −$1.50 |

- Conservative OE = OCF − capex − SBC. The maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) for FY2026 is −$214M — NI $655M + D&A $512M − capex $379M − ΔNWC $1,002M — in the same (negative) ballpark, so the FY2026 collapse is not a definition artifact.
- OE positive 2 of the last 3 fiscal years. SBC is trivial ($10–13M/yr); this is a capex-and-working-capital business, not an SBC story. Capex runs ~4.3–4.9% of revenue.
- **Base used = the engine's normalized base: median of the last 3 FY OE/share = $7.14/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). Rationale under BASE_DIVERGENCE below.
- **No TTM base is available:** ttm.py exits non-zero — no 10-Q has been filed since the 2026-05-31 fiscal year end (the first standalone quarter, in the transition period, had not been filed as of this run; next earnings are expected Oct 29, 2026 per press coverage). The FY2026 annual base is only ~4.5 months old (diagnostics: months_since_fy_end 4.53), so the median annual base stands.
- **The historical base overstates forward OE on one specific leg:** the carve-out years carried essentially no interest burden (interest expense $0 in FY2024 and FY2025, $57M in FY2026 per fundamentals.json) because the debt was issued at separation. Standalone guidance is ~$135M of interest expense for the seven-month transition period alone. Cash interest is paid out of OCF, so forward conservative OE will bear a cost the median base never did. This is handled through the scenario OE multipliers (base case 0.90 — see DCF), not through a base_override: any interest-adjusted base would need a run-rate interest figure that this run's computed outputs do not print, and the bounded-authority rule for base_override requires a construction built exclusively from those outputs.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: the densest LTL network in North America is a real scale asset and terminals are costly and slow to replicate, but LTL service is replicable by well-run rivals, pricing is cyclical, and FedEx Freight is not the service or margin leader — Old Dominion is.
- FOR: Largest NA LTL carrier by revenue ($8,782M in the 2025 industry ranking vs Old Dominion's $5,446M) — network density across 365+ locations / 26,000+ doors gives transit-time and coverage advantages (98% of U.S. ZIP codes); high barriers to entry — service-center terminals are costly and time-consuming to build, and the top five carriers collectively hold the majority of the market; dual Priority/Economy model lets it segment time-definite vs deferred freight off one network; proprietary digital platforms (LTL Select) and route-optimization tooling.
- AGAINST: Not the quality leader — Old Dominion has been ranked the top national carrier in shipper surveys for 16 consecutive years and earns structurally higher margins; FDXF's operating margin (fundamentals.json) fell 18.6% → 15.8% → 6.1% GAAP over FY2024–26 (FY2026 adjusted margin 12.6%, per the company release), all below best-in-class LTL levels; demand is industrial-cycle freight — average daily shipments fell 4% in FY2026 and 5.9% in Q4, with industry excess capacity pressuring yield; labor is the dominant cost and wage rates are rising; switching costs for shippers are low — freight is re-bid, and Estes, XPO, Saia and R+L run comparable networks.
- **ROIC evidence (fundamentals.json, roic_proxy): 62.5% (FY2024), 42.5% (FY2025), 9.9% (FY2026).** The first two prints are carve-out artifacts, not franchise proof: the denominator (equity + debt − cash) was the parent's small net investment in a business whose terminals and fleet were carried inside FedEx, and it bore no standalone debt. FY2026's 9.9% is the first print on a standalone capital base — and equity went negative (−$497M) after the debt-funded dividend, which makes the proxy itself unstable. Gross margin is not filed (no COGS tag in the carve-out statements — fundamentals.json gross_margin is null for all three years), so the margin evidence is the operating-margin series above: mid-to-high teens pre-spin, collapsing in FY2026. A moat above 5 would need demonstrated through-cycle ROIC on the standalone balance sheet, which does not exist yet — one of the reasons confidence is low.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5.4 final run (2026-10-16)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended growth is −3.40% (rev CAGR 5y −3.40%, 3y −3.40%, latest YoY −1.09%) — it is built entirely from the freight-recession carve-out years. It sits *below* what the company just printed and guided: Q4 FY2026 revenue +4.8% YoY ($2.4B, fuel surcharge and weight per shipment offsetting −5.9% shipments), and transition-period guidance of +4% to +6% revenue growth vs the $5.1B seven months ended Dec 31, 2025, with adjusted operating income guided to $605–645M vs $600M. A base-case start of −3.4% would contradict both the latest print and guidance with no written basis, so scenario starts were recalibrated upward via offsets (−0.046 / +0.004 / +0.064 / +0.094 / +0.134 vs g_base −3.40%): super bear −8%, bear −3%, base +3%, bull +6%, super bull +10%. The quality of the printed growth is weak (fuel/weight, not volume), which is why the base start (+3%) sits *below* the guidance range rather than inside it, and why bear-or-worse carries 40% of the probability.
**OE multipliers 0.65 / 0.80 / 0.90 / 1.00 / 1.15** — shifted down from the 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 defaults because the median base was earned with no standalone interest cost and no standalone overhead history; the base-case 0.90 is the interest-and-standalone-cost haircut described under Owner's earnings. Probabilities 15/25/30/20/10 — bear weight widened for the freight recession, the new leverage, and an unproven standalone cost base. Price $113.58.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −8.0% | 0.65 | Freight recession deepens; excess LTL capacity breaks pricing; levered OE squeezes | $24.53 | 4.87% |
| Bear | 25% | −3.0% | 0.80 | Volumes keep shrinking; wage growth eats yield gains; interest burden bites | $37.24 | 6.39% |
| Base | 30% | +3.0% | 0.90 | Guidance roughly delivered; slow volume recovery; margins rebuild toward low-teens | $53.83 | 8.44% |
| Bull | 20% | +6.0% | 1.00 | Industrial cycle turns; density and pricing discipline restore FY2024-25 OE on top of growth | $67.75 | 10.08% |
| Super bull | 10% | +10.0% | 1.15 | Full cycle upswing plus standalone cost-out; OE exceeds the carve-out peak and compounds | $91.91 | 12.76% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $51.88 (−54.3% vs price), IV@12% $68.36, IV@10% $86.68, weighted IRR 8.23%, base-case IRR 8.44%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Bear-case tier D (6.4%), bull-case tier C (10.1%) — see TIER_BAND. Diagnostics: OE yield 6.29%, terminal value 17.9% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.75x, net debt 4.24x normalized OE, 4.5 months since FY end.
- **Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted): 15% → $51.88, 20% → $36.99, 25% → $28.73.** Even the super-bull IV@15% ($91.91) sits below the $113.58 price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **THIN_HISTORY: only 3 fiscal years of data** — real and structural: the entire filed history is the carve-out prepared for the June 1, 2026 spin-off (10-K filed 2026-08-05). There is no longer standalone history to consult and no quarterly history at all (fundamentals.json assembled 0 quarters). Handled by confidence low, widened bear weight (40% bear-or-worse), and scenario sizing to the bear end.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share −1.50 vs 3-yr median 7.14** — the *latest* year is the distorted one. FY2026 absorbed $492M of separation and other costs (professional fees and an employee incentive plan associated with the spin-off, per the FedEx 10-K segment disclosure; FDXF reported FY2026 adjusted operating income of $1.1B vs $616M segment GAAP, a 25.6% adjusted decline, not a wipeout), the transfer of 1,500+ employees from Federal Express, higher wage rates, a lapped prior-year facility-sale gain, and a $1,002M ΔNWC outflow (financials_history.csv) as carve-out working capital normalized at separation — OCF fell to $167M from $1,531M while revenue fell only 1.1%. The median ($7.14) is corroborated by two independent years (FY2024 $7.14, FY2025 $7.25) at a stable level, so the median is the base; the known forward distortion in the *other* direction (new standalone interest, absent from all three history years) is handled in the OE multipliers, and the working-capital question — how much of the $1,002M swing recurs — is exactly what the first standalone 10-Q will answer.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.2x normalized OE** — the balance sheet from the filing: total debt $4,527M (debt_current $43M + debt_lt $4,484M, per financials_history.csv) against essentially no separately-held cash in the carve-out presentation, plus lease liabilities of $1,838M, total assets $6,884M, and **negative equity of −$497M**. The debt is not operating leverage gone wrong — it was issued at separation to fund the ~$4.1B cash dividend to FedEx — but it is real, permanent standalone leverage: guided interest of ~$135M for the seven-month transition period, against a normalized OE base of ~$1,068M/yr. A freight downturn now hits a levered equity. This is priced into the super-bear/bear multipliers (0.65/0.80) and the widened bear probability.
- **TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.4%) vs bull-case tier C (10.1%)** — the verdict spans tiers only at the low end; no scenario reaches B. Sized to the bear end: final tier D.

## My thoughts / overlay
- Method range: on the preliminary default run (defaults for probs/mults/offsets, growth start −3.4%) the weighted IRR was 7.83% with IV@15% $49.63 — Tier D. On this final run (guidance-checked growth, interest-haircut multipliers) it is 8.23% / $51.88 — Tier D. The defensible methods agree: this is a D at $113.58, roughly 2.2x the weighted IV@15%. The argument for the stock is not the DCF at this price; it is that a normalized mid-cycle OE well above the $7.14 median (FY2024-25 operating margins of 15.8–18.6% on a larger revenue base, plus standalone cost-out) eventually re-rates it — the super-bull case here still only reaches a 12.76% IRR.
- What would change the picture: (1) the first standalone 10-Q (expected with the Oct 29, 2026 earnings) — does OCF normalize after the separation working-capital swing, and what is the real standalone cost base? (2) Volume: shipments were −4% for FY2026 and −5.9% in Q4; revenue growth so far is fuel and weight, not freight. (3) The FedEx 19.9% stake overhang — monetization within 24 months is a known supply event. (4) Q4 FY2026 showed the trough shape: revenue $2.4B +4.8%, GAAP operating income $158M vs adjusted $363M — the gap between GAAP and adjusted is the separation-cost story, and it must actually close.
- Balance-sheet risk is the tail that matters: negative equity, $4,527M debt + $1,838M leases, and a cyclical revenue base. None of that is fatal for the largest LTL network in a normal cycle; all of it matters if the freight recession extends into 2027.
- Data notes (non-blocking enrichment): fundamentals.json carries 3 annual years and 0 quarters (no 10-Q yet), gross margin is null (no COGS tag filed), and the FY2024 balance sheet is largely untagged in the carve-out presentation (net debt null that year in fundamentals.json; the engine's history carries the FY2025 $73M → FY2026 $4,527M debt step-up). Enrichment: segments.json, statements.json, profile.json and street.json written; prices.py returned no price rows for FDXF (exit 2 — the price-history source has no series for the newly listed ticker), so reprice.py skipped by design and there is no live.json or prices.json. The score itself does not depend on either.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.23% on the v5.4 final inputs; bear D 6.4%, bull C 10.1% — sized to the bear end)
- Confidence: **Low** (3 carve-out years only, no standalone quarter filed yet, negative equity and brand-new leverage, ROIC history distorted by the carve-out capital base)
- One-liner: Largest North American LTL carrier with a real density moat (5/10), but a levered spin-off priced for a recovery it hasn't printed — at $113.58 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 8.2%, weighted IV@15% $51.88; hurdle price $51.88).
